newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen indices end down, caution persists.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen indices end down, caution persists.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices closed lower on Thursday amid continued caution over the upcoming 1997 interim results of listed firms, brokers said.
The B share index fell 0.75 points or 0.56 percent to 132.58 points on thin turnover of HK$34 million against Wednesday's HK$44 million.
The domestic A share index shaved off 10.79 points or 2.56 percent to 410.42 points, with turnover shrinking to 5.2 billion yuan from 7.7 billion yuan on Wednesday.
"People are waiting for interim results," a broker at J&A Securities (HK) Ltd said. "They would rather pull out of the market than engage in trading."
Listed firms must announce their 1997 interim results by the end of August but none of the 49 Shenzhen listed companies have yet released their figures.
Recent active trading on the Hong Kong stock market had resulted in the diversion of some funds out of Shenzhen-listed B shares, brokers said.
Some foreign investors were holding their funds to prepare for some forthcoming new B share issues in Shanghai and Shenzhen, the J&A broker said.
Brokers also said the B share market's performance would largely depend on A shares.
"B shares can not do well if A shares stagnate," an ayalyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Conglomerate China Vanke was the poorest performer, falling HK$0.44 or 7.69 percent to HK$5.28.
Brokers said sharp declines in market giant Shenzhen Development Bank exacerbated the A share retreat.
The bank share tumbled 2.04 yuan to 34.93 yuan, driven down by disappointment over the company's 1997 earnings prospect, brokers said.
Volume reached 17 million shares, making the bank the most actively stock.
Chemical fibre maker Searainbow Group, which was suspended from trading on Thursday morning, opened the afternoon session at its 10 percent limit-down at 8.74 yuan and stayed there towards the close.
The Bank of China on Thursday announced that it would sue Searainbow if it continued to delay repayment of a loan amounting to nearly US$16 million in balance and interest.
Searainbow said it was unable to repay the debt on time due to a bad investment and was trying to settle the issue.
"The company is facing a really big problem," a trader said.
